study_design: Prospective nested case-control study within the EPIC-Norfolk cohort
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Prospective phytoestrogen exposure was assessed using both biomarkers and estimates of intake in 89 British men recruited into the Norfolk arm of the European Prospective Investigation into Cancer and Nutrition study, men who subsequently developed prostate cancer. Results were compared with those from 178 healthy men matched by age and date of recruitment.
reason: The study compared prospectively assessed phytoestrogen exposure in men who subsequently developed prostate cancer with matched healthy controls. The abstract does not analyze an aggressive, advanced, high-grade, metastatic, or lethal incident endpoint.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Odds ratios for phytoestrogen exposure, as assessed using the four methods, were not significantly associated with prostate cancer risk (P = 0.15-0.94).
estimate_classifications.reason: This genistein/phytoestrogen row concerns overall prostate cancer risk, with no aggressive disease definition.
